messages:
lina: hey team quick one — my 22yo is starting a full-time role with benefits on 2026-09-01 and wants to enroll there. can i remove them from our plan effective 9/1? open enrollment closed. also wondering if premiums already taken for sept will be refunded, what happens to my FSA dependent-care elections, and whether this affects my HSA eligibility mid-year?

Diego (People Ops): hi @lina — congrats to your kid! this is a QLE (gain of other coverage) so yes you can remove the dependent. please upload either the new employer coverage letter or a benefits enrollment confirmation showing effective date (9/1/2026) to the portal: https://benefits.redwood.example/upload and pick "QLE - Other Coverage". We need that within 30 days of the event.

lina: uploaded their benefits_confirmation_sep2026.pdf. can removal be effective 9/1 or does it end 8/31? i'm worried about overlap and double coverage for a few days.

Priya (Benefits): thanks @lina — with proof we can set removal effective 9/1/2026 (same day the new coverage starts). Medical/dental/vision will end 8/31 at 11:59pm local time and termination will be processed to avoid paying for duplicate coverage after 9/1. if you prefer end-of-day 8/31 we'll do that, but we typically align to the new plan's effective date.

lina: and refunds? i saw premiums already taken for Sept in payroll yesterday. will that be reimbursed?

Marta (Payroll): i'll coordinate with benefits once the effective termination posts. if premiums were withheld for the pay period covering 9/01026, Payroll can issue a retro refund on the next payroll or apply a credit to the following pay date. small amounts default to a single refund; if it's >$500 we offer to spread it over 2 pay cycles per employee preference. tell us which you want when we post the amount.

lina: thx. what about Dependent Care FSA? my election still shows the full-year amount.

Priya (Benefits): Dependent Care FSA (DC-FSA) is different.

It depends on how you use it. If you already used funds for future care, removal reduces eligible dependents. We can pro-rate the remaining contribution allowance from 9/1 and adjust your election on a post-tax basis. Note: DC-FSA contributions are subject to use-it-or-lose-it rules; we recommend reconciling anticipated expenses now. We'll send an FSA adjustment form after termination posts.

lina: ok. how does HSA work if i was on family HDHP and switch to self-only? my contribution strategy was based on family max.

Priya (Benefits): HSA limits are based on coverage tier. If you move from family to self-only mid-year, the IRS pro-rata rule applies — you can only contribute the family maximum if you were family coverage for the entire last month of the year and on Dec 1 you still had family coverage. Otherwise your max is prorated across months you were family. We can provide a month-by-month breakdown once the enrollment change is finalized. Also you'll probably need to update payroll HSA deductions; Payroll can stop family-level contributions effective with the change.

lina: will my child's dependent-care receipts still be valid through Aug? i have recurring invoices for a camp in August that I already paid.

Priya (Benefits): receipts dated before 9/1 remain eligible. DC-FSA reimbursements are for eligible expenses incurred while the dependent was covered. Keep those receipts; we'll process claims per normal.

Diego (People Ops): next steps: 1) Benefits to approve termination on upload (Priya to confirm), 2) Payroll to compute refund/credit and HSA deduction changes (Marta), 3) we'll send confirmation message and any forms (FSA adjustment/HSA change). Target ETA 3 business days. cc @Marta @Priya. :spiral_calendar:

BenefitsBot: Auto-acknowledged upload received (benefits_confirmation_sep2026.pdf). Missing items: proof of employee relationship (if not on file). Please add if we don't already have dependent's SSN or matching record.

lina: uploaded dependent_ssn_card.jpg and a short note. thanks.

Priya (Benefits): all set on our side, termination approved effective 9/1/2026. we'll post the change tonight. you'll get a benefits confirmation email and digital ID status update.

Marta (Payroll): payroll note: we will credit the Sept premium on the 9/20 payroll (single refund). HSA contribution change will be effective with the next payroll after change posts; i'll DM you about the exact deduction amount and timing.

lina: appreciate it everyone. one last thing — will removing them trigger any COBRA notices for the dependent?

Priya (Benefits): good catch — COBRA rules vary by dependent type and state. For dependents who lose coverage due to gaining other coverage, COBRA continuation is sometimes optional. We'll generate any required notices and include instructions in your confirmation email. If they decline COBRA because they enroll elsewhere, record that for audit.

Diego (People Ops): closing loop: expect email confirmations and payroll refund details by end of week. ping here if you don't see them. :white_check_mark:
